This broke my dev environment as well. I have a reverse proxy running for dev. domain.
Returns a 500 Internal Server Error with this update 15.2.2.
Fixed by adding dev domain to allowedDevOrigins.
author: BrockWS

body: Thanks for the info, adding a warning here https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/77044 to make this more clear/easy to know what to configure.
author: ijjk

body:
> @ijjk Just as a heads up: This change is breaking for us, and we spent some time figuring out what's going on. It would be helpful if this could be mentioned in the docs or changelog in the future.

Same here - couldn't quite figure out why running my app through a proxy was breaking for me since 15.2.2 - any idea on how to run the app as a multi-tenanted system now, with dynamic proxy domains?
author: PodkopovP

body:
> Same here - couldn't quite figure out why running my app through a proxy was breaking for me since 15.2.2 - any idea on how to run the app as a multi-tenanted system now, with dynamic proxy domains?

You need to add the domains to `experimental.allowedDevOrigins` in your next config and it should work again
author: Mad-Kat

body:
> > Same here - couldn't quite figure out why running my app through a proxy was breaking for me since 15.2.2 - any idea on how to run the app as a multi-tenanted system now, with dynamic proxy domains?
> 
> You need to add the domains to `experimental.allowedDevOrigins` in your next config and it should work again

This does work, but will cause a bit of friction in our case as we work in a multi-tenanted system, meaning domains can be dynamic. It's not the worst thing in the world just adding a new domain to the config every time we want to test on a new domain, but ideally there would be a way to opt out of this feature.
author: PodkopovP

body:
> > Same here - couldn't quite figure out why running my app through a proxy was breaking for me since 15.2.2 - any idea on how to run the app as a multi-tenanted system now, with dynamic proxy domains?
> 
> You need to add the domains to `experimental.allowedDevOrigins` in your next config and it should work again

I have the same issue as @PodkopovP. Multi-tenant. Serving assets to  \*.localhost:3000 - Adding allowedDevOrigins: ["app.localhost:3000", "\*.localhost:3000"] doesn't solve the issue for me. Neither wild card nor explicit works.
author: alexanderbnelson

body:
> I have the same issue as @PodkopovP. Multi-tenant. Serving assets to  \*.localhost:3000 - Adding allowedDevOrigins: ["app.localhost:3000", "\*.localhost:3000"] doesn't solve the issue for me. Neither wild card nor explicit works.

`app.localhost` without the port should work and as I read the PR, the wildcard isn't supported.
author: Mad-Kat

body: 👋 This has broken cross-origin images in development (e.g. a remote embedded iframe is passed a localhost image URL -- https://github.com/cloudflare/stream-react/issues/106#issuecomment-2734443865), and `allowedDevOrigins` is not a valid workaround as CSS images cannot be marked as cross-origin...
author: MattIPv4

body:
> Initially I thought we could just bypass the cache generation process when in draft mode, but upon reflection, it does allow dynamic IO sync operations like `Date.now()` to work correctly, so I think this is still the best approach.

I changed my mind on this. Bypassing the cache entry generation completely, and with that also bypassing creating a `'cache'` work unit store, and therefore preserving the outer request store as work unit store, is the better approach, I believe. This allows us to retrieve the draft mode from the request store from within a `"use cache"` function. It also enables accessing other request-scoped data like cookies and headers, which I think we should allow when draft mode is enabled. So what I'm currently implementing is basically a mix of the initial attempt in this PR and the updated one, i.e. we're using Flight to serialize/deserialize the args and return value, but from a work unit store perspective we're treating it like it's request scope. Which also means that the following behavior is not really needed, because we only need it during prerendering:

> it does allow dynamic IO sync operations like `Date.now()` to work correctly
author: unstubbable

body:
>It also enables accessing other request-scoped data like cookies and headers, which I think we should allow when draft mode is enabled. 

This doesn't make much sense. In dev these caches would be errors so you would have to only conditionally access this data but to do that you'd need to read the draftmode state which is itself a request data and during a prerender should always be false. The nature of what is legit to read in a cache function isn't conditioned on the type of request you are doing the same way it is when you read this data in a request itself

body:
Those app router test failures are interesting — I'd argue that those aren't actually failures, but rather improvements. E.g. given an `appDir` GET request to `/api/app/1234/data`, I'd actually *prefer* spans named like [2] over [1]:

1. `GET /api/app/[param]/data/route` (current)
2.  `GET /api/app/[param]/data` (after this PR, notice this actually matches the HTTP pathname)

Considering that all `appDir` Route Handlers are provided by a `route.ts` file, the `/route` suffix is redundant. If that's how `appDir` spans are being named, I'm happy to knock off the redundant `/route` with this PR while I'm at it (and update the tests). Seems like that was the eventual intent anyways:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/e0abc5d2fa63b4da07e326815aab8927d072ec4c/packages/next/src/server/route-modules/app-route/module.ts#L737-L738

body:
Sorry if i'm wrong, as i'm not Next.js nor JavaScript expert but, from what i read from the code of this PR, it doesn't seem to be a proper fix to this problem.

If i understand code well, you added a some kind of a check (using randomly generated, let's say, password) if `x-middleware-subrequest` header is used by autheticated user - so, authenticated users are still able to use it to bypass _something_ (for example some kind of a permissions check middleware).
author: azurit

body:
@ijjk From what I see, a global variable is set to a random value here. Have the following two scenarios been considered in the fix?

1. Another unrelated request coming in between the time the value is set and the time the sub-request is coming in?
2. What about multi-instance server environments? How does this work here?

In both of these scenarios, is it okay for the mechanism to just "not work" and is the only downside some extra work being done by the server?
author: erkstruwe

body:
This will introduce a bug, where valid subrequests are dropped, if there is a runtime shift in e.g edge functions, as mentioned by @erkstruwe

Will try a setup tomorrow to verify the bug via a test repo

Furthermore crypto random might take a lot of time, as it waits for sufficient entropy especially on cold boot (otherwise up to a few milliseconds)

Possible solution would be a kind of configurable shared secret  (between servers) or possibly to generate it at build time (not sure on security implications)

author: samcx

body:
> @Marukome0743 Only the direction text (1., 2.) should be Geist Mono. Everything else should be Geist Sans.

Thank you for a nice review.

As you say, this PR changes the direction text (1., 2.) to Geist Mono.

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/fd5f588f43360913197f655a7322b37022c51e17/packages/create-next-app/templates/default-tw/js/pages/index.js#L26-L37

My PR adds the missing `${geistSans.className} ${geistMono.className}` classname.
Both `font-[family-name:var(--font-geist-sans)]` and `font-[family-name:var(--font-geist-mono)]` has been already declared.

On app router, `${geistSans.className} ${geistMono.className}` sets at [layout.js](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/create-next-app/templates/app-tw/js/app/layout.js).

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/fd5f588f43360913197f655a7322b37022c51e17/packages/create-next-app/templates/app-tw/js/app/layout.js#L19-L29

That's why the app router template correctly show the Geist fonts.

body: One way to make something deterministic is to serialize it twice. The first pass adds the `.status` and `.value` fields to the Promises, and then the second pass can synchronously serialize it in a single pass.
author: sebmarkbage

body: @sebmarkbage wouldn't doing it twice fail for arguments that are async iterables or `ReadableStream`s? AFAICT react doesn't stash the results on those (unlike promises which get `.status` + `.value`), so we'd end up trying to iterate over something that's already finished and crash

body:
This is still for ad-hoc debugging. It's only being added to enhance the logging made to the server console so that we can reproduce some particularly tricky errors related to partial prerendering in production.

I expect to remove it entirely if we don't find it useful and to pursue a more permanent solution if we find it really useful and/or required for using partial prerendering.

body:
Tracking only the most recently clicked link strikes me as the correct behavior, so it's good you thought about that, but instead of the timestamp logic you added, you can model this more explicitly using the Link instance object: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/7b301075c207427868da2b126ceb4d3229a00978/packages/next/src/client/components/links.ts#L18-L34

These instances are already created for the purpose of visibility tracking.

I think the implementation would be roughly something like this:

- Add a `linkForCurrentNavigation: LinkInstance | null` variable somewhere in the global app's state. Conceptually this isn't React state; it's external/global state, because we only access it during event handlers, not during rendering.
- Whenever a navigation occurs, update the link's optimistic pending state to `true`, and also update the current `linkForCurrentNavigation`'s state to `false` to turn it off. Then update the variable to the new LinkInstance (or `null` if it was triggered by `router.push()`.
